searchText: Is there some kind of social consensus among core devs that an attack would be made against bad behaving validators? Has there been some historical talk about this scenario that I could read about? I could see that kind of modifications are highly controversial eg, a government could order that a validator (eg, Coinbase) are not allowed to process transactions by those that are on US sanctioned list. Would core devs deploy a fork that would slash all Coinbases validators? It has been discussed, and some of us have been trying to get a bit of an unofficial commitment from the core devs about whether they would write code against and/or support a fork that wiped out censors after the fact. It sounds like a bit slippery slope on what is defined as censoring and what is not Yes, but the alternative is worse (allowing censorship to go unchecked). <@415548822983278593> had what I thought was a relatively bright line, which was "a group of validators that intentionally reorgs the chain or refuses to sign over valid blocks". well, if there are still enough non censoring validators, things should be fine ah, right if they do reorging too
